context: Your firm prepaid a full year of insurance on July 1st. Your fiscal year ends December 31st. The policy runs July 1 through June 30.
question: How should this insurance expense be recorded?
option_a: All in the year it was paid (Year 1)
option_b: All in Year 2 when the policy expires
option_c: Half in Year 1 (July-Dec) half in Year 2 (Jan-June)
explanation: Match expense to the revenue it helps generate. The insurance enables operations for 6 months in Year 1 (July-Dec) and 6 months in Year 2 (Jan-June). Split 50/50 across the two periods.

context: Your retail store used electricity in December. You receive and pay the bill in January.
question: In which period is the utility expense recorded?
option_a: January — when the bill is received
option_c: December — when the electricity was used
explanation: The electricity was used IN December to keep the store open and generate December revenue. Match the expense to December. The payment date is irrelevant under accrual accounting.

context: Your firm spent $2 million on research and development this period. The R&D may or may not generate future products.
question: When is the R&D expense recorded?
option_b: Spread over the expected useful life
explanation: R&D cannot be matched to specific future revenue because (a) it is uncertain if revenue will result and (b) we do not know when. When you cannot match to revenue recognize the expense IMMEDIATELY. R&D is always expensed as incurred.

context: Your employees worked the last week of December. You will pay them on January 4th.
question: When is the wage expense recorded?
option_b: December — when the work was performed
explanation: The employees performed work IN December generating December revenue. Match the wage expense to December — the period they worked. Under accrual accounting you record an accrued liability in December even though cash goes out in January.

context: Ford sold a car two years ago. Today they pay $800 to replace a faulty transmission covered under the original warranty.
question: In which period was the warranty EXPENSE recorded?
option_a: Today — when the repair is made
option_b: Last year — midpoint of warranty period
option_c: Two years ago — when the car was sold
explanation: Ford estimated warranty costs at the time of the sale (two years ago) and recorded that expense to match with the car revenue. The actual repair today uses the warranty liability already established. Expense was in the year the car was sold.

context: A customer paid $3000 for an extended 3-year warranty on a car they purchased separately after their original warranty expired.
question: How is this extended warranty REVENUE recognized?
option_a: All at once when the customer pays $3000
option_b: Spread evenly over 3 years as time passes
option_c: Only when warranty repairs are actually made
option_d: Immediately — it is a separate transaction
explanation: An extended warranty is a separate performance obligation satisfied over time. Recognize $1000/year over the 3-year period as the protection service is provided — just like insurance or a service subscription.
